answer: A bonded escrow mechanism resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital deposits before participating in market bids, such as trading survey data of a coral reef, seismic scans of oil shale, or telemetry from a distant nebula. An attacker incurs the verifiable financial cost and liquidity loss of tied-up capital per identity. However, this barrier marginalizes underfunded legitimate agents and remains vulnerable to well-capitalized adversaries.
